$comment: Written exceptions for scripts/check-sdk-parity.ts, which FAILS the process on any violation not listed here. An entry is { rule, key, reason } and nothing else; `key` is the violation identity the report prints, and `reason` must be at least 20 characters saying WHY parity stops here. An entry whose violation no longer reproduces fails the gate as stale: the PR that binds the route is the one that deletes its excuse and lowers `baseline`. `baseline` may only go down on its own; raising it is a visible diff a reviewer must accept, because it means a new route shipped with no client behind it.
$waves: The waves named in these reasons are the SDK binding waves of PRODUCT-1820 step 4: each wave moves one family of routes behind a @houston/sdk module, so naming a wave says which family a route belongs to. A1 org, A2 spaces, A3 teams, A4 account, B1 workspaces, B2 agent library, B3 board, C1 routines, C2 skills, C3 integrations, C4 credentials/providers, C5 files, D1 chat/turns. A1-A4, B1-B3, C1-C3 and C5 are bound, and a route of theirs that still has no SDK method says below what keeps it unbound; C4 and D1 are the two waves that have not shipped.
